_evidence: MEASURED (config.json + one safetensors header; the local/global structural-identity claim and the tied-embedding claim both verified from tensors, not from config fields). Zero mlx/torch load, zero HCLI resident contention.
_label: Odyssey I DISCOVERY. FIRST encoder-only specimen this session -- a masked-LM encoder, not a generative decoder. Fourth independent test of R-tied-embedding-dedup-verify.

structural_category.family: encoder-only masked language model. Every other specimen surveyed this session is either decoder-only (Qwen3, iLLaDA, RWKV7, mamba3-siso, BitNet, LFM2, Dream-v0) or encoder-decoder (whisper), or not a language model at all (pi0, sam2.1, evo2). No autoregressive generation loop at all -- one forward pass produces all positions.

LOCAL_GLOBAL_ALTERNATION_COSTS_ZERO_BYTE.verified: a global layer and a local layer carry BYTE-IDENTICAL tensor structure (same names, same shapes) -- confirmed by comparing their full signatures, not inferred from the config.
LOCAL_GLOBAL_ALTERNATION_COSTS_ZERO_BYTE.finding: the heterogeneity is a RUNTIME ATTENTION-MASK POLICY, not a weight difference: most layers attend within a 128-token window and every 3th attends globally, at zero additional stored bytes. This is a DIRECT CONTRAST with LFM2-24B-A2B earlier this session, whose conv-vs-attention heterogeneity is expressed in genuinely different tensors and therefore does cost bytes. Two routes to heterogeneous attention: one paid for in storage, one free. A Gravity allocation rule keyed on 'layer type' must know which kind it is looking at -- for this body there is nothing type-specific to allocate differently.

TIED_EMBEDDING_FOURTH_TEST.finding: tie_word_embeddings=true AND no separate head tensor exists -- so unlike iLLaDA-8B and Qwen3-0.6B (both of which physically duplicate the tied matrix on disk), this checkpoint stores it once, as pi0_base does. R-tied-embedding-dedup-verify now stands at 4 specimens, 2 wasteful / 2 clean -- confirming it is a per-checkpoint PACKAGING CHOICE, not a family or framework property. The rule's value is the VERIFY step: the flag alone predicts nothing.

byte_accounting_EXACT.dtype: F32 throughout -- THIRD F32 specimen this session (pi0_base, sam2.1-hiera-large, now this). All three are non-generative or non-decoder bodies, while every decoder-only LM surveyed shipped BF16/F16. Suggestive, not established: n=3 and the causal story (release convention vs precision requirement) is untested.

obvious_representation_opportunities: F32 storage on a 395M-param encoder is the obvious first lever: a bf16 cast alone would halve the 1510 MiB footprint. Untested here.

Because local and global layers are structurally identical, there is no organ-type split to exploit -- any heterogeneous-precision scheme would have to be keyed on measured per-layer sensitivity, not on architecture, which is a strictly harder search than the MoE-organ splits this session has used.
failure_modes_not_yet_tested: No capability battery (would need a masked-LM / retrieval / classification benchmark, outside Hawking's generative Doctor batteries).
No measurement of whether the global layers tolerate less compression than the local ones -- the one genuinely interesting sensitivity question this architecture raises.
preliminary_disposition: RESEARCH SPECIMEN. Cheap, structurally novel for this census (first encoder-only), and it contributes a real methodological correction: heterogeneity visible in a config is not necessarily heterogeneity in the weights.

preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.resident_candidate: NOT APPLICABLE as a Resident -- an encoder-only masked LM cannot run HCLI's WorkUnits, which require generation and tool calls.
preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.cepheid_candidate: PLAUSIBLE IN PRINCIPLE, UNTESTED: an encoder is a natural fit for an independent SCORER/calibrator role (embedding or classifying candidate outputs) rather than producing them -- the one Star role this body could conceivably hold. Not evaluated here, and per S003 deterministic/formal checks may still be superior.
preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.verdict: Odyssey I discovery only; the Cepheid angle is flagged as a question, not a claim.
